result_text:
Suppliers now have payment terms in days. They default to 30, you can set them at registration, and you can change them later. The full test suite passes. I didn't add a new test for the 45-to-14-days example.

- **`schema.sql`**: new column `supplier.payment_terms_days`, not null, default 30, must be 0 or more.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new field `paymentTermsDays`. I kept the old five-argument constructor, which uses the standard 30 days. The existing callers and tests therefore compile unchanged and get 30 days.
- **`SupplierStore.java`**: `create` and `update` write the new column, so terms can be set at registration and changed on renegotiation. The listings (all by name, by country, by minimum rating) and `findById` now return it.
- **`Rows.java`**: `Rows.supplier` reads the column, so it appears wherever a supplier is read. That includes the supplier performance and spending reports and the categories-with-a-single-supplier listing.
- **`PurchaseOrderStore.java` and `StockStore.java`**: I added the column to the two other queries that load a supplier (the supplier purchased-quantity report and the purchase suggestions).
